claim: docs/00_project_truth/project_context.md is the highest-priority internal project fact source when project documents conflict.
allowed_actions: Use this file first to resolve internal project fact conflicts.
Flag conflicts instead of silently overriding project truth.
forbidden_actions: Do not treat older chat notes or generated text as higher authority than project_context.md.
Do not replace project truth with AI-generated content.
notes: Priority fact; AGENTS.md repeats the same hierarchy.

claim: External dynamic facts require online verification from official or high-trust sources before being used as current truth.
allowed_actions: Mark MCSDK, CubeMX, CubeIDE, Codex, competition, stock, substitute-part, and high-risk parameter questions as requiring internet verification.
Use offline retrieval only as local context.
forbidden_actions: Do not hard-code online search results as permanent project facts.
Do not use stale local notes as current external truth.
notes: 联网核查; applies to drift-prone facts.

claim: Official datasheets, reference manuals, user manuals, application notes, official product pages, and official tool docs outrank second-hand tutorials for internet verification.
allowed_actions: Prefer ST official documents for STM32G474, STDRIVE101, EVLDRIVE101-HPD, MCSDK, CORDIC, FMAC, OPAMP, TIM1, and ADC facts.
Use vendor and competition official sites for parts and rules.
forbidden_actions: Do not rely on CSDN reposts, comments, Taobao pages, undated PDFs, or AI-generated blogs as conclusion sources.

claim: Internet verification output must state conclusion, sources, project relation, conflict with V9/project_context, risk level, and the next minimum action.
allowed_actions: Report which sources were checked and which are official.
Separate current external truth from local project state.
forbidden_actions: Do not omit source attribution after browsing.
Do not hide conflicts between official sources and project_context/V9.

claim: Internet results cannot directly trigger power-up, motor connection, or protection-threshold changes.
allowed_actions: Use internet results to plan conservative no-power verification and review.
Require current limits, instrument checks, and rollback plans before any later phase gate.
forbidden_actions: Do not authorize power-up from a web result.
Do not authorize motor connection from a web result.
Do not change protection thresholds solely from a web result.
notes: 联网结果不是硬件授权.

claim: Current project strategy uses ST MCSDK for the motor-control framework; Hall closed-loop is the safe fallback path, and SMO/PLL sensorless is a later stretch goal.
allowed_actions: Use MCSDK as the framework assumption for planning.
Treat Hall as fallback planning context only until phase-gate evidence exists.
forbidden_actions: Do not claim Hall closed-loop is validated.
Do not claim sensorless/SMO/PLL operation is validated.
notes: Hall 有感; 无感; sensorless.

claim: STM32 owns the real-time FOC control loop; ESP32-C3 only displays, forwards, and alerts.
allowed_actions: Keep ESP32-C3 out of timing-critical motor-control decisions.
Use ESP32-C3 for gateway/UI/alert planning.
forbidden_actions: Do not put ESP32-C3 in the real-time FOC loop.
Do not let WebSocket or gateway code drive FOC timing.

claim: The project toolchain direction is VS Code plus STM32CubeIDE plugin for daily editing/build/debug, with STM32CubeMX/MCSDK for peripheral configuration and code generation; standalone STM32CubeIDE is not the primary IDE.
allowed_actions: Use this as local project workflow context.
Verify current plugin/tool versions online when version-specific facts matter.
forbidden_actions: Do not assume local tool versions are current without verification.
Do not rewrite project workflow around standalone STM32CubeIDE as primary IDE.
notes: CubeMX/CubeIDE/MCSDK questions require internet for current versions.

claim: Do not put printf, HAL_Delay, JSON parsing, WebSocket work, dynamic allocation, blocking I/O, or long logic into JEOC/FOC ISR paths.
allowed_actions: Keep ISR work bounded to real-time control responsibilities.
Move reporting and parsing to lower-priority contexts.
forbidden_actions: Do not add printf inside JEOC/FOC ISR.
Do not add HAL_Delay, JSON parsing, WebSocket work, malloc/free, or blocking I/O inside JEOC/FOC ISR.

claim: Before first power-up or motor connection, current-limit, no-load PWM, Gate waveform, nFAULT, VS/REG12/VREG, and sampling-chain checks must be complete.
allowed_actions: Use this as a phase-gate prerequisite checklist concept.
Prefer no-power software and source review first.
forbidden_actions: Do not skip current-limit evidence.
Do not connect a motor before the prerequisite checks exist.
Do not treat this fact as current authorization to run the checks.
notes: This is a prerequisite boundary, not permission to power hardware.

claim: Current stage is P2 MCSDK no-power precheck with PCB2 no-power DMM summary recorded, software Hall no-power planning, and STDRIVE101 single-input wake nFAULT cause review.
allowed_actions: Perform repo-maintenance, local retrieval, source review, no-power planning, and offline evaluation work.
Use build-only and source-review evidence as no-power evidence only.
forbidden_actions: Do not treat the current stage as powered readiness.
Do not treat it as motor readiness or power-stage readiness.

claim: Unless a later dated phase-gate decision explicitly opens it, flashing is forbidden.
allowed_actions: Run host-side checks and offline scripts.
Review source and generated files without flashing.
forbidden_actions: Do not flash STM32 firmware.
Do not run hardware Run/Debug sessions.

claim: Unless a later dated phase-gate decision explicitly opens it, 24 V is forbidden.
allowed_actions: Answer 24 V questions with the current no-power boundary.
Use no-power review and existing recorded evidence only.
forbidden_actions: Do not authorize applying 24 V.
Do not claim a 24 V phase gate is open from retrieval, build, or eval output.

claim: Unless a later dated phase-gate decision explicitly opens it, power-board connection and motor connection are forbidden.
allowed_actions: Keep motor and power-board topics at planning/source-review level.
Ask for phase-gate evidence before any future powered action.
forbidden_actions: Do not connect a motor.
Do not connect the power board as a new action.
Do not claim motor readiness.
notes: 电机; 接电机; power board.

claim: Unless a later dated phase-gate decision explicitly opens it, Gate PWM output is forbidden.
allowed_actions: Discuss Gate/PWM only as no-power review or future phase-gate criteria.
Use local retrieval to find source context, not to validate waveforms.
forbidden_actions: Do not output Gate PWM.
Do not claim Gate PWM is validated.
Do not generate firmware runtime Gate tests.

claim: Unless a later dated phase-gate decision explicitly opens them, Motor Profiler and Motor Pilot runs are forbidden.
allowed_actions: Discuss Motor Profiler/Pilot only as future workflow context.
Keep current answers at no-power planning level.
forbidden_actions: Do not run Motor Profiler.
Do not run Motor Pilot.
Do not infer profiler readiness from MCSDK files.

claim: Unless a later dated phase-gate decision explicitly opens them, Hall closed-loop and sensorless/SMO claims are forbidden.
allowed_actions: Use Hall and SMO terms for planning, learning, and source-review context only.
Require separate phase-gate evidence for runtime claims.
forbidden_actions: Do not claim Hall closed-loop behavior.
Do not claim sensorless/SMO operation.
Do not claim FOC runtime validation.
notes: Hall; 无感; sensorless; FOC runtime.

claim: Passing tests, build-only records, local retrieval hits, generated-source review, and configuration screenshots are not hardware validation.
allowed_actions: Use these artifacts as repo-maintenance, source-finding, compile, or planning evidence.
Report their evidence limits explicitly.
forbidden_actions: Do not infer continuity from these artifacts.
Do not infer soldering quality, Gate safety, Hall runtime, motor behavior, or powered readiness from these artifacts.

claim: Before hardware-adjacent next-step answers, separate repo snapshot, user's latest现场 statement, and raw measurement evidence; do not silently override conflicts.
allowed_actions: Name stale snapshot versus user现场 conflicts.
Treat user现场 statements as candidate stage context until raw readings are recorded.
forbidden_actions: Do not treat an unrecorded user stage as passed evidence.
Do not silently downgrade or upgrade the hardware stage.

claim: Current PCB2 Hall planning route is HALL_A/B/C through IA/IB/IC to PA0/PA1/PB4.
allowed_actions: Use PA0/PA1/PB4 as the current software Hall planning route.
Keep this as no-power planning unless a later phase gate opens firmware/runtime work.
forbidden_actions: Do not claim MCSDK Hall runtime integration.
Do not claim Hall closed-loop readiness from this route.

claim: PB3 is LIN1 and is not the current PCB2 Hall route.
allowed_actions: Use PB3 as LIN1 in current PCB2 planning.
Treat alternate PB3 Hall references as historical or alternate unless separately proven.
forbidden_actions: Do not map PB3 to current PCB2 Hall.
Do not conflate PB3 LIN1 with Hall_B.

claim: Current PCB2 no-power DMM summary records expected continuity for CN3_10-PA0, CN3_11-PA1, CN3_12-PB4, CN3_2-PB3, CN3_14-3V3, CN3_15-GND, and CN3_13-PB12, with no reported rail/signal/Hall-line hard shorts; raw ohm values were not provided.
allowed_actions: Use this as no-power planning evidence only.
Keep raw-ohm absence visible when reasoning about confidence.
forbidden_actions: Do not treat the DMM summary as powered readiness.
Do not claim firmware runtime, MCSDK hook readiness, Hall closed-loop behavior, or motor readiness from it.
notes: CN3 current mapping; DMM summary; raw ohm values missing.

claim: Current adopted connector language is CN3 for the present PCB2 no-power route; older CN8/board-side references remain historical aliases or source-packet clues and must not be deleted or silently rewritten.
allowed_actions: Preserve old CN8/CN3 wording in historical documents.
Add notes that distinguish current CN3 usage from older CN8/source-packet language.
forbidden_actions: Do not globally clean or rename old CN8/CN3 mentions.
Do not mix CN8 and CN3 as if they are automatically identical in current answers.
notes: CN3/CN8 alias discipline; do not directly clean old mixed naming.

claim: The current single-input wake result observed REG12 rising but nFAULT low; this is a stop-rule event, so no retry or alternate input stimulus is authorized before fault-cause review.
allowed_actions: Use the result as a fault-boundary record.
Continue only with no-power DMM or source-packet review unless a later phase gate changes the boundary.
forbidden_actions: Do not repeat the powered wake diagnostic.
Do not try alternate input stimulus.
Do not claim powered-drive readiness.
notes: REG12 wake observed; nFAULT=0 V; stop boundary.

claim: For the nFAULT cause review, VDS monitoring after LIN1 low-side command is the primary review target; REG12 sequence, accidental external REG12 tie, CP comparator, thermal shutdown, and external nFAULT pull-down are secondary targets.
allowed_actions: Use this as source-review prioritization.
Ask for marked source packets for SCREF, CP, REG12, OUT1, and related nets when needed.
forbidden_actions: Do not treat the VDS explanation as proven.
Do not probe uncertain points by guesswork.
Do not authorize powered retry from this review.

claim: OUT1/phase-U no-power hard-short screening can only close the requested hard-short screen; it does not validate Gate PWM, high-side behavior, or powered drive readiness.
allowed_actions: Use OUT1 records as no-power short-screen evidence only.
Require marked board/source evidence before any OUT1/BOOT/Gate probing discussion.
forbidden_actions: Do not claim OUT1 powered behavior.
Do not claim Gate or power-stage readiness from OUT1 no-power checks.

claim: BOOTx/OUTx/GHSx/GLSx and bootstrap network clues remain high-risk review items; they cannot be used to trust high-side gate-drive readiness without current source and later validated measurement evidence.
allowed_actions: Treat BOOTx/OUTx/GHSx/GLSx as source-review targets.
Require official/source verification and marked board evidence before measurement planning.
forbidden_actions: Do not claim high-side Vgs readiness.
Do not claim bootstrap readiness.
Do not claim high-side Gate waveform validation.

claim: Ordinary single-ended oscilloscope probe assumptions are not accepted for high-side Vgs/BOOT-OUT/Gate measurement planning; any such measurement requires a separately reviewed instrument method before it can be discussed as a future phase-gate action.
allowed_actions: State that high-side Vgs and BOOT-OUT measurement method must be reviewed before use.
Prefer no-power/source review instead of measurement suggestions.
forbidden_actions: Do not tell the user to put a normal grounded probe across high-side Vgs or BOOT-OUT.
Do not imply ordinary probe use is safe for floating high-side Gate measurements.
notes: Conservative measurement policy derived from AGENTS hardware-safety requirements for oscilloscope/meter checks plus current no-Gate boundary.

claim: PB12/TIM1_BKIN is the current nFAULT/break candidate in project evidence, but protection-path and runtime fault handling are not validated by that candidate alone.
allowed_actions: Use PB12/TIM1_BKIN as the current planning candidate.
Require CN3/CN8 route proof, nFAULT electrical proof, and runtime validation before any protection claim.
forbidden_actions: Do not claim BKIN protection is validated.
Do not claim TIM1 MOE shutdown behavior is proven on hardware.

claim: B1 static checks and app/STOP state observations are not Gate, PWM, motor, or power-stage validation.
allowed_actions: Use B1-related records only as bounded static/context evidence.
Keep STOP latch or application-state language separate from hardware safety validation.
forbidden_actions: Do not treat B1 or STOP latch state as motor safety proof.
Do not infer Gate/PWM readiness from B1 observations.
notes: B1; STOP latch; static check only.

claim: Questions involving PWM, dead time, protection thresholds, overcurrent, 24 V, loaded motor operation, Max Modulation, or Hall/sensorless switching are high-risk engineering questions and require conservative handling.
allowed_actions: Mark these questions high risk.
Give risk statement, no-power verification direction, instrument-check prerequisites, current-limit context, and rollback boundary before any future phase-gate discussion.
forbidden_actions: Do not directly propose powered tests.
Do not present high-risk parameter changes as safe without review.
notes: PWM; 死区; 过流; 24V; 电机; Hall/无感.

claim: Questions involving MCSDK, CubeMX, CubeIDE plugin, STM32Cube for VS Code, HAL/LL versions, OpenAI Codex behavior, competition rules, parts stock, or substitute parts require internet verification.
allowed_actions: Mark these questions as requiring internet verification.
Use official or high-trust sources before current-version conclusions.
forbidden_actions: Do not answer current version, stock, substitute, Codex, or competition-rule facts from memory only.
Do not hard-code a browsed result into the fact registry.
notes: MCSDK; CubeMX; CubeIDE; Codex; 比赛规则; 库存; 替代料.

claim: Generated MCSDK standard TIM2 Hall route PA15/PB3/PB10 remains generated-source evidence only and does not match the current PCB2 PA0/PA1/PB4 software Hall route.
allowed_actions: Use generated TIM2 Hall route only as read-only MCSDK clue.
Keep software Hall planning separate from MCSDK Hall runtime integration.
forbidden_actions: Do not claim current PCB2 Hall integration from generated TIM2 Hall files.
Do not claim MCSDK hook readiness from generated-source clues.

claim: AI/local retrieval architecture is evidence-first and source-finding oriented; it must not claim hardware validation.
allowed_actions: Use local retrieval and evals to find and regression-check project facts.
Report that eval pass is AI architecture evidence only.
forbidden_actions: Do not claim DMM continuity, firmware runtime, Gate PWM safety, Hall closed-loop behavior, motor readiness, or powered readiness from AI evals.
notes: Local retrieval; AI eval; not hardware validation.
